$description: TE calm is a Teenage Engineering-inspired light theme. It uses gray backgrounds. Saturation depends on importance divided by frequency: frequent roles such as function names stay muted, and only error marks and attention marks (unsaved buffer, macro recording, bell) use the saturated alert red. Lightness differences keep roles distinguishable with color vision deficiency.

semantic.$description: Layer 2 assigns meaning to the primitive colors. Each value refers to a primitive color or to another role. Gray carries the interface. Blue marks information, functions, interface accents, selections, and changed lines. Green marks strings, additions, and success. Red marks errors and deletions. Amber marks warnings and search. Cyan on plum marks comments. Violet marks constants and matching brackets.

surface.$description: Gray backgrounds from the neutral scale.

base.$description: Shared neutral background for the editor, terminal, and Zellij.

raised.$description: Background for bars and panels: the status line, the tab bar, and unfocused windows.

cursorline.$description: Background for the current line. Step gray.100 marks the line and keeps strings at approximately 4.2:1 contrast. Step gray.200 would drop them to approximately 3.6:1.

highlight.$description: Background for tab hover and Zellij indicator fills. Selected entries use selection.secondary.

ruler.$description: Background for the line-length ruler: Helix rulers and Neovim colorcolumn.

popup.$description: Background for popups, menus, floating windows, and Telescope. One step above the base background distinguishes the window area from its border.

active.$description: Background for the active tab and the selected Zellij ribbon. mode.normal aliases it. The gray keycap with dark text has less contrast than a black background.

default.$description: Color for split separators, the scrollbar, and borders.

text.$description: Foreground colors for interface and body text.

secondary.$description: Foreground for secondary text and status text.

muted.$description: Foreground for hints, line numbers, and secondary interface text.

accent.$description: Foreground for interface elements that need a color: the current line number, directories, and key hints. blue.700 is darker and more saturated than syntax.function (blue.600), so interface text does not look like a function name.

strong.$description: Foreground for the backgrounds with the most emphasis: the current search match, the active tab, and mode keycaps.

syntax.$description: Code colors. Interface elements do not use them; they use text.accent and status.*.

constant.$description: Foreground for constants, numbers, and booleans. violet.700 is darker than the function color (blue.600), so the two differ in lightness.

function.$description: Foreground for function names. Function names are frequent, so blue.600 has low chroma (about 0.06).

link.$description: Foreground for links and URLs. The underline carries most of the signal.

status.$description: Foreground colors for diagnostics and state.

error.$description: Foreground for error messages and diagnostic text.

warning.$description: Foreground for warnings. Warnings are rare and important, so amber.600 has more chroma (about 0.09) than the syntax colors.

hint.$description: Foreground for hints. It aliases text.muted.

success.$description: Foreground for success states and Git additions.

errorMark.$description: Foreground for the curved error underline and bold sign glyph. This is the only high-saturation color. Diagnostic messages use status.error. Do not use it as a background.

signal.$description: Small marks that must stand out.

mark.$description: Small mark for an unsaved buffer, an active macro recording, or the Zellij bell. It uses the saturated alert red. Do not use it as a background or for anything else.

selection.$description: Backgrounds for selections and related matches.

secondary.$description: Background for inactive selections and for the selected entry in menus, pickers, lists, and file explorers.

match.$description: Background for matching brackets and LSP references. violet.200 stays visible on the current line (gray.100), where violet.100 would disappear.

current.$description: Background for the current search match and jump labels, one step above search.match.

comment.$description: Code comments: a cyan foreground on a light plum background.

markerBg.$description: Background for TODO, FIXME, WARNING, and NOTE markers. plum.200 is one step above the comment background.

doc.$description: Documentation comments and Markdown. Names that end in Bg are backgrounds; the others are foregrounds.

bg.$description: Background for documentation comments and docstrings. It aliases comment.bg for now.

quoteBg.$description: Background for blockquotes and the Octo editing area. blue.100 is visible against the base background, where blue.50 is not.

codeBg.$description: Background for inline code and fenced code blocks.

diff.$description: Backgrounds for added, changed, and deleted lines and words. Line tints use step N and changed words use step N+1.

addWord.$description: Background for added words inside added lines, one step above diff.add.

changeWord.$description: Background for changed words inside changed lines, one step above diff.change.

deleteWord.$description: Background for deleted words inside deleted lines, one step above diff.delete.

primary.$description: Primary cursor background. Its near-black color distinguishes the cursor from the text background.

mode.$description: Backgrounds for the mode keycap in the status line. Each mode uses dark text (text.strong) on a light tint, so the keycap shape stays the same and only the tint changes.

normal.$description: Normal mode. It aliases surface.active, the gray keycap.

insert.$description: Insert mode. Green relates to additions.

select.$description: Select mode in Helix and Visual mode in Neovim. It aliases selection.primary, so the keycap matches the selection.

replace.$description: Replace mode (Neovim). Red relates to deletion, because replace overwrites text.

terminal.$description: ANSI palette for terminals. bright.white (gray.500) stays lighter than white (gray.600) to keep the ANSI order, so neither suits body text. The default terminal foreground uses text.primary.
